::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Easter [5 April 1885]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Harry Ransom Humanities Research Center, University of Texas, Austin
:::

My dear [Mr Wither](people/person_1544.qmd)

It has been a beautiful day Easter day, full Church and 104 Communicants – 50 early and 54 late – not quite so many as last year, but [Frances](people/person_1604.qmd) was in bed with neuralgia and [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd) is at Arlington. We had scarcely enough primroses for the Church, they are so late this year – but there were plenty of daffodils and it looked very well

No, [Mildred Coleridge](people/person_17.qmd) has not married [Adams](people/person_12.qmd) nor do I think she will marry him.[^1]

It is altogether the most extraordinary and miserable business I ever heard of, and my poor [Mary](people/person_351.qmd) is quite heartbroken about it.

[Mrs George Heathcote](people/person_1690.qmd) is at the Park and came over on Wednesday to see [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd)

Your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The Hon. Mildred Coleridge, niece of CMY's great friend Mary Coleridge, married Charles Warren Adams, against the wishes of her family, on the 24 June 1885.
